1.note: In modern editions this passage is Antiquities 3.7.1–7 (3.151–187); the author's numbering follows the chapter division of the edition he used.

2.note: The phrase is unclear; the sense of Josephus (the ends hang down) suggests 'toward the ground'.

3.note: Transliterated; Josephus says the Hebrews call the plant *saccharon*. The Hebrew spelling may reflect a Latin or Italian form of that name, but the identification is not certain. The Greek name is hyoskyamos (henbane).

4.note: In modern editions the Alexander–Jaddua episode is Antiquities 11.8.5 (11.331); the number is kept as the author gives it.

5.note: In modern editions this description is War 5.5.7 (5.235); the reference is kept as the author gives it.

6.note: Josephus says the letters are 'four vowels'; the author renders this as the four letters that are the elements of the sound of our speech.
